title: Which three dates in a column add to fifty one?
description: Three dates one below the other on a calendar page add to fifty one. The dates are written with the letter eigh, the sum is made into an equation, and the dates are found and checked. Keeko doubts that the dates are seventeen, eighteen and nineteen.
teaching_notes: One idea: dates one below the other go up by seven each step, so they are eigh, eigh plus seven and eigh plus fourteen. Watch for students who let the dates go up by one, as they do along a row.

source: A friend picks three dates one below the other on a calendar
video_script.why: A child writes three dates in a column of a calendar with one letter, forms an equation from their sum, and finds the dates.
video_script.substitution: three dates one below the other on a calendar page, with the sum fifty one and the letter eigh for the top date
video_script.anchor: a calendar page with three dates in one column shaded and the words the sum is 51
video_script.wrong_answer: the dates are seventeen, eighteen and nineteen
video_script.wrong_move: lets the three dates go up by one, as they do along a row, instead of by seven down a column
video_script.payoff_line: The dates are ten, seventeen and twenty four.

final_answer.spoken: the dates are ten, seventeen and twenty four

maths_rules: Top date a; the dates below are a + 7 and a + 14.
Doubt: 17, 18, 19 sit side by side in a row and add to 54, not 51.
video_script.design: One idea: going down a column adds seven each time. The calendar page stays in the anchor band and the equation sits on the working board.

<bookmark mark='cal'/>The friend says their sum is fifty one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which three dates did the friend pick?

narration: <bookmark mark='down'/>A week has seven days, so the date below is seven more.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Two steps down is seven more twice, which is fourteen more.

beats.on_screen: Given: three dates one below the other on a calendar; their sum is 51

marks.given: the column of three dates and the sum 51 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three dates one below the other on a calendar. Their sum is fifty one.

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the three dates that the friend picked from the calendar page.

marks.dates: a, a + 7 and a + 14 are written in the column

narration: <bookmark mark='dates'/>Step one, call the top date eigh. The dates below it are eigh plus seven and eigh plus fourteen.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The three dates add to three eigh plus twenty one.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>Step two, three eigh plus twenty one equals fifty one.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take away twenty one from both sides, and three eigh is thirty.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Divide both sides by three, and eigh is ten.

marks.dates: the dates 10, 17, 24 are written in the column

narration: <bookmark mark='dates'/>Step three, with eigh equal to ten, the next dates down are seventeen and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check, ten plus seventeen plus twenty four is fifty one.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The dates are ten, seventeen and twenty four.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand; Keeko's bubble shows 17, 18, 19; those dates light up side by side in one row, not in a column; 17 + 18 + 19 = 54 is written beside 51; the bubble is struck out

marks.test: 17, 18 and 19 light up side by side in one row and 17 + 18 + 19 = 54 is written beside 51

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.
<bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the dates are seventeen, eighteen and nineteen, because dates in a line go up by one.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it. Those dates sit side by side in a row, and they add to fifty four.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That is not fifty one. Down a column, the dates go up by seven.
